request.deadline: 12 months from deployment; month-6 yield distribution; wind-down reconciliation within 30 days if triggered
deliverables: Deploy treasury-owned liquidity into Strike Finance V2 USDM liquidity infrastructure
Return realized yield from the first six months to the Cardano Treasury at month 6
Return 100% of remaining treasury-owned deployed assets plus remaining realized yield at month 12, minus any realized losses in a wind-down scenario
Provide monthly public transparency reports covering deployment status, utilization, volume, P&L, yield, drawdown, stablecoin exposure, risks, and deviations
Provide third-party assurance reports at deployment confirmation, month-6 distribution, and month-12 return
request.recipient: independent multisig council composed of Rami from Snek, Phil from Surf, and James from Monetra/Moneta, administering a Strike Finance liquidity deployment
request.what: 12-month productive deployment of Cardano treasury assets into Strike Finance V2 liquidity infrastructure, with ADA sold for USDM stablecoin liquidity.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 9,000,000 ADA for a 12-month liquidity deployment rather than grant funding.
The deployed ADA will be sold for USDM, modeled at ADA = 0.15 USD to create approximately 1,350,000 USDM of stablecoin liquidity.
The proposer models a 10% USD-denominated annual return, equal to about 135,000 USD or 900,000 ADA-equivalent in annual yield, but states returns are not guaranteed.

Strike reports more than 1.13 billion USD in cumulative volume, roughly 968,000 to 1,001,000 trades, over 3,000 unique traders, more than 1.16 million USD in protocol revenue, and over 3.25 million USD in liquidity provider profit.
The proposer states Strike accounted for more than 50% of Cardano trading activity over the past six months.
The document provides V2 launch-to-2026-06-15 metrics including 87,288,044 USD total V2 volume, 410,800 total V2 trades, 2,681 users, and 30,105 USD total V2 revenue.
Operational custody is proposed to be held by an independent multisig council, and Strike Finance is stated not to have unilateral custody or control of treasury assets.
The proposal identifies risks including ADA appreciation underperformance, USDM depeg or redemption risk, smart contract risk, yield underperformance, custody risk, and operational multisig risk.

Governance review is proposed if drawdown exceeds 8%, reporting is missed for two consecutive monthly cycles, or unresolved custody, accounting, stablecoin, redemption, or smart contract concerns arise, with mandatory review at 10% drawdown and a separate wind-down trigger above 20% drawdown.
The proposal states Strike V2 has undergone unofficial reviews and that an official audit by Christian Schmitz is expected by July 1, 2026, but no completed audit report is included in the document.

summary: The document proposes a temporary 9,000,000 ADA treasury-owned liquidity deployment into Strike Finance V2 via USDM, administered by an independent multisig council, with modeled yield, reporting, assurance, and return-of-funds commitments, but many key performance, custody, audit, market, and budget claims are asserted without attached references.
